title: Vector Quantization (VQ-VAE)
tagline: Replace a continuous latent with the nearest entry of a learned discrete codebook
summary: VQ-VAE swaps the continuous latent of an autoencoder for a discrete one: every encoding snaps to the nearest of K learned code vectors, so the latent is really just an integer index. Drag the encoding point z and watch it jump to its nearest code z_q, drag the codes to redraw their Voronoi territories, and quantize a whole cloud of points at once to see the assignment. A closing section explains the straight-through estimator that lets gradients flow back through the hard argmin.
highlights: Drag the encoding point z and watch the snap arrow jump to z_q, the nearest code vector.
Drag the K code vectors and see the Voronoi cells — each code's territory — redraw live.
Quantize a whole cloud of encodings at once, each coloured by the code it is assigned to.
Read the quantization error and the log2(K) bits it takes to store a discrete index.
See how the straight-through estimator copies the gradient from z_q back to z so the encoder can still learn through a non-differentiable argmin.
